abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic cancer remains a highly lethal malignancy with limited therapeutic options. Rhein, a natural anthraquinone, exhibits anti-tumor potential, yet its molecular targets in pancreatic cancer are poorly understood. This study aimed to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanism of rhein in pancreatic cancer.
METHODS: Bioinformatic analysis using the GSE101448 dataset and machine learning identified matrix metalloproteinase 9 (MMP9) as a core target of rhein and pancreatic cancer. The MMP9 and transcription factor AP-2 alpha (TFAP2A) protein levels were assessed using Western blot. Cell viability, proliferation, and migration were assessed using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8), colony formation, and wound healing assays, respectively. Cell apoptosis was measured using flow cytometry. Measurement of lactate production, glucose consumption, and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) levels was performed using corresponding assay kits. The binding between TFAP2A and the MMP9 promoter was predicted by JASPAR and verified using chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) and dual-luciferase reporter assays. The interaction between rhein and TFAP2A was investigated via molecular docking. The effect of rhein on tumor growth was explored in xenograft models.
RESULTS: MMP9 expression was inhibited by rhein treatment in pancreatic cancer cells (P < 0.05). Rhein treatment promoted cell apoptosis and inhibited colony formation, migration, and glycolysis, which were reversed by MMP9 overexpression (all P < 0.05). Furthermore, MMP9 overexpression impaired the inhibition of rhein on tumor growth in a mouse model. Mechanistically, Rhein inhibited TFAP2A to downregulate MMP9 transcription. Rhein exerted anti-tumor effects by inhibiting the TFAP2A/MMP9 axis. TFAP2A overexpression inhibited cell apoptosis and promoted migration and glycolysis in rhein-treated cells, which were remarkably abolished after MMP9 knockdown (all P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Rhein exerted anti-tumor effects by inhibiting the TFAP2A/MMP9 axis, providing a promising therapeutic agent for pancreatic cancer.
key_points_ko: 라인(rhein) 처리는 췌장암 세포에서 MMP9 발현을 유의하게 억제했습니다 (P < 0.05).
라인은 세포 사멸을 촉진하고 세포 집락 형성, 이동, 당분해를 억제했습니다 (모두 P < 0.05).
동물 모델 실험에서 라인은 종양 성장을 억제하는 효과를 보였습니다.
summary_ko: 이 연구는 천연 안트라퀴논 유도체인 라인(rhein)이 췌장암 세포에 미치는 항암 효과와 그 분자적 기전을 밝히고자 했습니다. 연구진은 생물정보학 분석과 실험을 통해 라인이 TFAP2A/MMP9 축을 억제함으로써 암세포의 생존, 이동, 당분해(glycolysis)를 저해하고 세포 사멸을 유도한다는 사실을 확인했습니다. 또한 동물 모델(xenograft model)을 통해 라인이 종양 성장을 억제함을 입증했습니다. 초록에 환자 수나 구체적인 생존기간 수치는 명시되지 않았습니다.
title: Rhein suppresses pancreatic cancer progression and glycolysis by inhibiting the TFAP2A/MMP9 axis: An integrated bioinformatics and experimental study
